name: Left wing
summary: In Bobbio's account the left is defined by egalitarianism: the conviction that people are more equal than unequal and that most inequalities are social and can be removed, expressed in social rights such as education, work and health care. Noël and Thérien likewise read the left-right divide as a long clash over equality, which survey respondents tie to redistribution and the role of the state. The family divides on liberty, between moderate wings that accept democratic rules and extremist wings that do not.
scope: The left as a positional family, answered only from comparative scholarship that defines it (Bobbio on left and right; Noël and Thérien on the left-right divide as a debate over equality). No member movement's programme or thinker answers for it, so socialism, social democracy, communism and anarchism are not used. Most statements are null because these sources define the left by one criterion (equality) and a few corollaries.
